stem: Which pairing matches the course summary’s global/local planning distinction?

options.text: Both terms describe nearby reactive planning, differing only in whether the objective is time or distance.
Global planning uses the known full map; local planning reacts to recent nearby observations.
Global planning reacts to nearby observations; local planning first computes the whole-map route.
Both terms describe whole-map planning, differing only in whether the path is a grid or a graph.
